pr_title: drivers: usb: dc_sam0: Handle suspend interrupt
pr_body:
For the SAM0 USB peripheral, the USB device suspend interrupt occurs
when the device is disconnected from a host.

This interrupt must be handled and reported to the USB subsystem in
order to allow the USB subsystem to free any context-specific resources
(e.g. cancellation of pending USB transfers).

Signed-off-by: Stephanos Ioannidis <root@stephanos.io>

Fixes #26656

Tested on `atsamd21_xpro` and `atsame54_xpro`

NOTE: This implementation enables the suspend interrupt on-demand, instead of permanently enabling it, because that is what ASF does (ASF implements a sort of interrupt enable status "state machine", which we will eventually have to implement in this driver anyway in the future).
pr_comments:
> I'd like to play with enabling the interrupts up front vs on event. Any ideas why ASF does it this way? I'm reluctant to just copy the behavior without understanding it.

@nzmichaelh I tried enabling interrupts upfront and that seemed to work at first glance (didn't do any exhaustive testing though), but I am quite certain ASF is not taking the more convoluted approach without a good reason:

https://github.com/adafruit/asf4/blob/d270f79aa16dd8fd4ae3b6c14544283dcb992e9c/samd51/hpl/usb/hpl_usb.c#L982-L984
https://github.com/adafruit/asf4/blob/d270f79aa16dd8fd4ae3b6c14544283dcb992e9c/samd51/hpl/usb/hpl_usb.c#L992-L994

My first guess on why ASF does this is that there are certain conditions in the USB core logic that may lead to spurious interrupts, but without any detailed information on the peripheral internals, any guess would be as good as mine.

Unless we can be completely sure, we should take the conservative approach and follow the manufacturer reference implementation (i.e. ASF).

> Unless we can be completely sure, we should take the conservative approach and follow the manufacturer reference implementation (i.e. ASF).

Understood.  I guess I've dealt with too many poor quality BSPs in the past :)

LGTM with a comment explaining why this is done on mode change instead of at initialisation.
Going to implement full suspend-resume support here after https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/26725 is resolved.

issue_context.title: SAM0 USB transfer slot leak
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
"No transfer slot available" error message is displayed and USB transfer stops working when repeatedly unplugging and re-plugging the USB cable on the SAM0-family SoCs.

This bug has been confirmed on the SAM D21 and E54 SoCs using `atsamd21_xpro` and `atsame54_xpro`, respectively.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build and flash `samples/subsys/usb/cdc_acm`
2. Unplug and re-plug the USB device cable for 4 times.

**Expected behavior**
USB transfer slots are properly cleaned up.

**Impact**
USB is unusable.

**Logs and console output**
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.3.0-809-g897b5bf60a12  ***
[00:00:00.005,000] <inf> cdc_acm_echo: Wait for DTR
[00:00:00.431,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
<REPLUG>
[00:00:13.350,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
<REPLUG>
[00:00:16.301,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
<REPLUG>
[00:00:19.575,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
<REPLUG>
[00:00:26.076,000] <err> usb_transfer: No transfer slot available
[00:00:26.076,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.11.3
 - Commit SHA: 897b5bf60a12e71976df6885817aff04b09a33ea

**Additional context**
Note that USB status callback for "suspend" event is not invoked, which is almost certainly the reason why the transfer slots are not de-allocated when un-plugging.

This issue is not reproducible on `sam_e70_xplained` (SAM-family SoC), which has the suspend event callback properly working.
```
[00:01:00.808,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device suspended
[00:01:05.564,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
[00:01:07.276,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device suspended
[00:01:08.973,000] <inf> usb_cdc_acm: USB device configured
```
comments: The bug is also reported here  #21234 and has an PR #24402
This issue is clearly not a duplicate of #21234; at most, it is related.

review_comments: nit: the comment doesn't add any new information.  Change to why the interrupt is disabled at this point or drop.
It will be handled even if the suspend interrupt is disabled. And yes please help to save the planet remove unnecessary comments (less storage consumption).

> It will be handled even if the suspend interrupt is disabled.

My observation is that the suspend interrupt still occurs even if it is disabled **when the device is re-plugged**; but, in order to get the suspend (as in detach) interrupt when you actually unplug, you must enable this interrupt here.

> please help to save the planet remove unnecessary comments (less storage consumption).

You must be very environmentally conscious. Are you powering your workstation with a bike generator too? :)

nit: the comment doesn't add any new information.  Explain why this is happening or drop.

Also, as this starts adding state based interrupt selection, could you log a tracking bug and reference it from here as a TODO?
nit: the comment doesn't add any new information so drop
Please recheck, resume (EORSM) has to be handled to (always suspend+resume). No need to enable/disable them conditionally.

> Please recheck, resume (EORSM) has to be handled to (always suspend+resume).

This PR is solely intended to address the lack of any "disconnect" event handling, which leads to USB transfers not being cancelled when disconnected; EORSM (and others) can be addressed in #24402.

> No need to enable/disable them conditionally.

As far as I can see, there is no need, but this is what ASF does, so I am going to follow what ASF does.

See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/24402#discussion_r450040877

>This PR is solely intended to address the lack of any "disconnect" event handling, which leads to USB transfers not being cancelled when disconnected; EORSM (and others) can be addressed in #24402.

But it is not just a detach event, the host (host conroler) can put the device to suspend (7.1.7.6 Suspending "Devices can go into the Suspend state from any powered state.").

> But it is not just a detach event, the host (host conroler) can put the device to suspend (7.1.7.6 Suspending "Devices can go into the Suspend state from any powered state.").

As I previously mentioned, this PR only addresses handling of the suspend interrupt in the context of "detach"/"disconnect" event in order to fix the issue described in #26656.

Since SAM0 USB core implicitly handles (that is, automatically acknowledges) all disabled interrupts, handling wakeup and/or resume interrupts (note that there are two and you seem to be referring to the WAKEUP interrupt, not EORSM here) do not necessarily have to come in conjunction with handling of the suspend interrupt; hence, I consider that out of scope for this PR.

As I noted above in the PR description, we will eventually need to address the rest of the interrupts (WAKEUP, EORSM, SOF, ...) as well, but that is the story for another PR.

Once again, this PR is a critical bug fix for #26656, not a feature enhancement.

Once again, SUSPEND is not a detach event and you have to implement RESUME too, this is **mandatory** for the stack and you patch does not fix the bug (or maybe it introduces a new one), the atsamr21-xpro for example still hard-faults after few suspend events from the host. That may work for you because you plug and unplug the cable and the host resets and re-enumerates the device. This will not go in how it is.

> SUSPEND is not a detach event

well, it clearly functions like one on the SAM0 SoC -- do you know any other way to detect detach/disconnect event on it because I would really appreciate it if you could tell me?

> you patch does not fix the bug

I am starting to wonder if you actually took time to read this PR and #26656 because it clearly is a fix for the aforementioned (rather critical) bug.

> the atsamr21-xpro for example still hard-faults after few suspend events from the host.

That has always been the case and this PR is clearly an incremental fix to what is a critical issue that renders USB useless on SAM0 SoCs.

> This will not go in how it is.

My intention was to make this PR a bug fix for #26656, a not feature enhancement; but if you insist that this becomes one, then I would be more than happy to make it one.
